title: The rise and fall of Rome
intro: Step through a thousand years of Roman history. Highlighted shapes come from an approximate historical reconstruction (historical-basemaps), not surveyed borders. Ancient frontiers were zones of control rather than precise lines.

steps.label: c. 500 BCE
steps.title: A city-state in central Italy
steps.text: Rome has recently become a republic (traditionally 509 BCE) and controls only a small area of Latium, surrounded by Etruscans, Latins and Italic peoples.

steps.label: c. 300 BCE
steps.title: Mastering Italy
steps.text: Through wars and alliances with neighbouring peoples, the Roman Republic comes to dominate central and southern Italy.

steps.label: c. 200 BCE
steps.title: Victory over Carthage
steps.text: After the Second Punic War (218–201 BCE), Rome controls Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica and parts of Spain, and becomes the leading power of the western Mediterranean.

steps.label: c. 100 BCE
steps.title: A Mediterranean power
steps.text: Carthage and Corinth were destroyed in 146 BCE. Rome now rules Greece, North Africa around Carthage and much of Spain, but the Republic is torn by civil strife.

steps.label: 1 BCE
steps.title: The empire of Augustus
steps.text: Caesar's conquest of Gaul and the annexation of Egypt (30 BCE) have made the Mediterranean a 'Roman lake'. Augustus rules as the first emperor.

steps.label: c. 100 CE
steps.title: Near the peak
steps.text: Under Trajan the empire reaches its greatest extent by his death in 117 CE, from northern Britain to Mesopotamia, ruling perhaps 50–60 million people.

steps.label: c. 300 CE
steps.title: Crisis and the Tetrarchy
steps.text: After a century of civil wars and invasions, Diocletian splits authority among four rulers. The reconstruction shows the empire divided into their zones.

steps.label: c. 400 CE
steps.title: East and West
steps.text: From 395 CE the empire is permanently divided into a Western and an Eastern (Byzantine) half, each with its own emperor.

steps.label: c. 500 CE
steps.title: The West falls, the East endures
steps.text: The last Western emperor was deposed in 476. Germanic kingdoms now rule the West, while the Eastern Roman Empire continues from Constantinople until 1453.

sources.title: historical-basemaps (A. Ourednik et al.), GPL-3.0 — approximate reconstruction
